title: Elementary Mathematics II (Calculus)
description: The calculus and trigonometry course, taught as MAT 121: Calculus and Trigonometry before the CCMAS codes: functions and the circular functions, trigonometric identities and equations, limits and continuity, differentiation and its applications, techniques of integration, and definite integrals and areas. Built from the MAT 121 lecture notes, Ini Adinya's MAT 121 integration lectures (2021) and the past papers from 2007/08 to 2014/15, labelled with the former code.

topics.title: Functions and the Circular Functions
topics.summary: A function assigns one value to each input and can be given by a rule, a graph or a set of ordered pairs. The circular functions sine, cosine and tangent, and their reciprocals, are defined on the unit circle, are periodic and are odd or even.
subtopics: Sine and cosine on the unit circle; radians
tan, sec, cosec, cot; odd and even functions

topics.title: Trigonometric Identities and Equations
topics.summary: Trigonometric identities come from the Pythagorean relation and the addition formulae. They give double angles, product-to-sum formulae and the form R sin(x + α), which is used to solve equations such as a sin x + b cos x = c.
subtopics: Writing a sin x + b cos x as R sin(x + α)
Solving trigonometric equations and general solutions

topics.title: Limits and Continuity
topics.summary: The limit of f(x) as x approaches a is the value f(x) gets close to as x gets close to a. Limits are found by factorising, rationalising, dividing by the highest power, or using lim sin θ/θ = 1, and they define continuity.
subtopics: The limit sin θ/θ = 1 and related limits

topics.title: Differentiation
topics.summary: The derivative is the limit of the gradient of a chord, f'(x) = lim (f(x + h) − f(x))/h. Students find derivatives from first principles and with the sum, product, quotient and chain rules, including trigonometric, exponential, logarithmic and implicit functions.
subtopics: Derivatives of sin, cos, sec, eˣ and ln x

topics.title: Applications of Differentiation
topics.summary: Derivatives give tangent lines, approximations and small errors, rates of change and the turning points of curves. The second derivative test separates maxima from minima, and these tools combine in curve sketching.
subtopics: The second derivative test and inflexion

topics.title: Techniques of Integration
topics.summary: Integration reverses differentiation: an indefinite integral is the family of antiderivatives F(x) + C. Students integrate by standard forms, substitution, partial fractions, trigonometric identities and substitutions, and by parts with reduction formulae.
subtopics: Integration by parts and reduction formulae

topics.title: Definite Integrals and Areas
topics.summary: A definite integral ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx = F(b) − F(a) measures the area under a curve. Its properties split and reverse intervals, and it gives areas between curves and distances travelled in motion problems.
subtopics: Integration as the area under a curve
